name: Aqua Gravel
summary: A natural mixed-colour gravel in browns, greys and tans. It works for streambed details, filling gaps around stones or as a coarser foreground accent.
bestFor: Adding texture and a natural riverbed look to the foreground of a planted tank.
highlights: Natural rounded gravel in mixed earthy colours
Useful for streambeds and detailing around rock

specs.Effect on water: Inert
specs.Prep: Rinse before use

watchOut: Too coarse for carpet plants to root in, so use it as an accent rather than a planting substrate.

name: Colorado Sand
summary: A natural sand with a light sandy-beige tone, a touch warmer than La Plata Sand. It suits paths and foregrounds where you want a more natural, riverbed feel.
bestFor: Nature-style and riverbank layouts that want a softer, warmer foreground than white sand.
highlights: Good for paths, beaches and open foreground areas

specs.Effect on water: Inert
specs.Prep: Rinse before use

watchOut: Like any cosmetic sand, it will mix into soil unless the two are kept apart.

name: La Plata Sand
summary: A fine, pale natural sand used for paths, foreground patches and beach areas in nature aquariums. Its light colour brightens the front of a layout and contrasts well with dark aqua soil.
bestFor: Iwagumi and nature aquarium layouts that need a clean, bright foreground or path.
highlights: Classic choice for sand paths and open foreground areas

specs.Effect on water: Inert
specs.Prep: Rinse before use

watchOut: Keep it separated from soil with stones or a divider, or the two will mix over time.

name: Accent Driftwood
summary: Assorted small-to-large natural driftwood pieces sold in packs. They are meant for finishing touches: stacking at the base of a hardscape, wrapping with moss, or holding a few epiphytes.
bestFor: Filling gaps and adding detail around an existing hardscape rather than as a main piece.
highlights: Four size bands from about 5 cm to 64 cm+
Useful for layering and finishing details

specs.Effect on water: Releases tannins, lowers pH slightly and tints the water
specs.Buoyancy: May float at first
specs.Prep: Soak (or boil small pieces) until waterlogged; weigh down if it floats

watchOut: Assorted wood types, so pieces will not always match each other.

name: Amazon Wood
summary: Mid-sized driftwood with knots, grooves and varied branching that combines the textures of several popular woods. Pieces fit together easily into larger wood layouts.
bestFor: Tanks of about 40 litres and up that need several matching pieces for a larger wood build.
highlights: S, M and L sizes, about 20-51 cm
Knots and grooves for moss and rhizomes

specs.Effect on water: Releases tannins, lowers pH slightly and tints the water
specs.Buoyancy: Not stated; soak before use
specs.Prep: Soak (or boil small pieces) until waterlogged; weigh down if it floats

name: Ancient Stone
summary: A grey and brown stone in the same family of looks as Manten and Yama stone. Its angular, weathered shapes suit Iwagumi and it also makes a solid base under wood.
bestFor: Iwagumi keepers who like the Manten look and want a slightly darker, more angular stone.

specs.Effect on water: Not stated by the seller; do a vinegar fizz test and check KH/GH before use
specs.Prep: Rinse and scrub well before use

name: Ashen Stone
summary: A pale, almost white stone with a smooth surface and rounded shapes. It gives a clean, minimal look and suits river layouts and bare-bottom tanks.
bestFor: Minimal or river-style scapes that want bright, soft stone against lush green planting.
highlights: Smooth and rounded, no sharp edges
Good for goldfish and other delicate-finned fish

specs.Effect on water: Not stated by the seller; do a vinegar fizz test and check KH/GH before use
specs.Prep: Rinse and scrub well before use

watchOut: Pale stone shows algae and diatoms quickly, and white stones are often limestone, so test it.

name: Basin Driftwood
summary: An ornamental driftwood with deep grooves, dips and bowl-like hollows. Those basins are perfect for tucking in Anubias, Buce or clumps of Java Fern.
bestFor: Focal-point wood in nature layouts heavy on epiphytes.
highlights: S, M and L sizes, about 25-51 cm+ long

specs.Effect on water: Releases tannins, lowers pH slightly and tints the water
specs.Buoyancy: Usually sinks on its own in about two weeks
specs.Prep: Boil or soak to speed waterlogging

watchOut: Priced higher than most woods in the range.

name: Black Forest Spider Wood
summary: A dark, charcoal-brown spider wood that keeps getting darker over time, unlike normal spider wood which starts pale. It releases little tannin and has the same twisting, root-like branches.
bestFor: Moody, dark scapes where you want branchy wood that contrasts with bright plants.
highlights: Nano, S and M sizes from about 3 cm to 41 cm
Twisting root-like branches for moss and epiphytes

specs.Effect on water: Releases only a little tannin
specs.Buoyancy: Floats at first; soak or weigh down
specs.Prep: Soak (or boil small pieces) until waterlogged; weigh down if it floats

name: Black Lava Rock
summary: Classic porous black lava rock, sold in a 15 to 16 lb lot. It is light, so you get a lot of volume per kilo, and the rough surface is one of the easiest for moss and epiphytes to grab.
bestFor: Budget-friendly builds, nano tanks and moss-covered scapes that need plenty of stone volume.
highlights: Excellent for moss, Anubias, Bucephalandra and ferns
Easy to break into smaller pieces

specs.Effect on water: Inert
specs.Prep: Rinse and scrub well before use

watchOut: Rough edges can catch long fins, and it holds debris, so rinse it thoroughly first.

name: Black Lava Rock Cave
summary: Single pieces of black lava rock with one or more natural holes through them. Turn the opening forward for a shrimp or fish cave, or upward and fill it with soil for a little planted pocket.
bestFor: Shrimp and nano tanks that need hiding spots, or scapers wanting planted pockets at different heights.
highlights: Four sizes from about 15 cm to 30 cm across
Porous lava gives grip for stacking and for moss
Handy for nano tanks and small caves for shy fish and shrimp

specs.Effect on water: Inert
specs.Prep: Rinse and scrub well before use

watchOut: Rough surface can snag long fins, and hole size and position vary between pieces.

name: Black Mountain Seiryu Stone
summary: A near-black Seiryu variety with blue undertones and the same grooves and jagged forms as the classic grey stone. The dark colour makes bright green and red plants stand out.
bestFor: Iwagumi and nature layouts where you want Seiryu shapes in a darker, moodier colour.
highlights: Charcoal to almost black with a blue tinge

specs.Effect on water: Raises KH, GH and pH (calcareous, like all Seiryu-type stone)
specs.Colour: Charcoal to near black, blue undertone
specs.Prep: Rinse and scrub well before use

watchOut: Raises hardness like normal Seiryu, so skip it for Caridina or soft-water fish.

name: Black Ridge Stone
summary: A layered, jagged stone in dark charcoal and earthy brown, with tiny reflective flecks that catch the light. The irregular ledges stack well into slopes and cliff faces.
bestFor: Layered mountain or tide-pool style scapes where you want to build height with stacked ledges.
highlights: 30 lb (about 13.6 kg) box of varied sizes
Charcoal and brown tones with a subtle glint under LEDs
Rugged, layered edges for slopes and terraces
Good ledges for moss and rhizome plants

specs.Effect on water: Not stated by the seller; do a vinegar fizz test and check KH/GH before use
specs.Colour: Dark charcoal and earthy brown with fine flecks
specs.Prep: Rinse and scrub well; the seller advises against boiling

name: Black River Slate
summary: Flat dark grey slate that looks almost black underwater. Good for cave stacks, paths and moss stones, or as a base under intricate wood work.
bestFor: Dark-toned layouts and cave stacks where you want slate that disappears into shadow.
highlights: Dark grey to near black when wet
Flat pieces for stacking and paths
Easy to split for moss wrapping

specs.Effect on water: Inert
specs.Colour: Dark grey, near black when wet
specs.Prep: Rinse and scrub well before use

name: Black Slate
summary: Black and grey slate with small white striations. The flat profile makes it easy to stack into caves and terraces, and it splits readily for paths and moss-wrapped accents.
bestFor: Cave builds, terraces and moss stones in any size of tank.

specs.Effect on water: Inert
specs.Colour: Black and grey with fine white streaks
specs.Prep: Rinse and scrub well before use

name: Black Star Lava Rock
summary: Rounded, pebble-like lava rock that is much smoother than regular lava while keeping its porous surface. You still get lots of volume per kilo and a good home for moss and bacteria.
bestFor: Tanks with bettas or fancy goldfish, or anyone who wants lava's benefits without sharp edges.
highlights: Porous surface for moss and epiphytes

specs.Effect on water: Inert
specs.Prep: Rinse and scrub well before use

name: Blue Mountain Seiryu Stone
summary: A darker, medium-grey Seiryu with a blue tinge and pale veins running through it. It gives more contrast than classic Seiryu while keeping the same sharp, grooved character.
bestFor: Iwagumi scapes in hard or moderately hard water that want Seiryu shapes with a cooler colour.
highlights: Medium-dark grey with blue tinge and light veins
Well priced for a Seiryu variety

specs.Effect on water: Raises KH, GH and pH (calcareous, like all Seiryu-type stone)
specs.Prep: Rinse and scrub well before use

watchOut: Hardens water like other Seiryu, which matters for soft-water shrimp.

name: Bonsai Driftwood Trees
summary: Hand-built bonsai trees made from natural driftwood, each numbered design offered in two to five sizes. Tie moss onto the fine branch tips and you have a mature-looking tree scape within weeks, with no wood carving or gluing.
bestFor: Bonsai and tree-style layouts where you want a finished focal piece sized to your tank, from 20 litre nanos to large displays.
highlights: 20 numbered designs, most in S, M and L
Sizes run from palm-sized nano trees to a 1.2 m long display piece
Fine twig canopy ready for moss or Riccia
Many designs sit on a heavy base that helps them stay put

specs.Effect on water: Releases tannins, lowers pH slightly and tints the water
specs.Colour: Warm brown trunk, pale twig canopy
specs.Texture: Natural driftwood with fine branch tips
specs.Buoyancy: Buoyant until waterlogged; soak or weigh down
specs.Prep: Soak until it sinks; run carbon or change water if tannins bother you

name: Brook Stone
summary: A deep grey stone with white striations and jagged texture, in the same style as Ryuoh and Seiryu. It gives strong contrast against bright plants.
bestFor: Iwagumi layouts that want a dark, striated Seiryu-style stone.

specs.Effect on water: Not stated; Seiryu-like stones often raise KH and pH, so test before use
specs.Prep: Rinse and scrub well before use

name: Caledonia Stone
summary: A marbled grey, brown and cream stone that sits somewhere between Seiryu and Elephant Skin. Pieces tend to be chunky and boulder-like, good for height or for borders.
bestFor: Layouts that need tall, chunky stones rather than flat or pointed ones.
highlights: Marbled grey with brown and cream
Useful for building borders and retaining edges

specs.Effect on water: Not stated by the seller; do a vinegar fizz test and check KH/GH before use
specs.Prep: Rinse and scrub well before use

name: Chameleon Stone
summary: A dark charcoal stone with rounded knobs and pockets, a bit like a denser take on volcanic rock. The gaps and crevices are handy for wedging in Bucephalandra, Anubias and moss.
bestFor: Island, cliffside or dark Iwagumi scapes where you want a black-grey rock with lots of texture for epiphytes.
highlights: 30 lb (about 13.6 kg) box of mixed pieces
Deep charcoal and grey colour that makes greens pop
Knobbly, craggy shapes with natural planting gaps

specs.Effect on water: Not stated by the seller; do a vinegar fizz test and check KH/GH before use
specs.Prep: Rinse and scrub well; the seller advises against boiling

watchOut: Single 30 lb option only, and one of the pricier stones per kilo in this range.

name: Cholla Driftwood Tree
summary: Branching cholla cactus skeleton with a hollow core and holes all over. It grows biofilm that shrimp and snails graze, gives fry places to hide, and slowly softens the water.
bestFor: Shrimp tanks and fry-rearing setups where grazing surface and hiding spots matter more than looks.
highlights: S and M sizes, about 25-61 cm
Hollow and holey, great shrimp cover

specs.Effect on water: Releases tannins slowly, can lower pH and soften water slightly
specs.Buoyancy: Floats until waterlogged
specs.Origin: Cholla cactus skeleton (south-west USA and Mexico)
specs.Prep: Soak (or boil small pieces) until waterlogged; weigh down if it floats

watchOut: Softer than true driftwood and breaks down over a year or two.

name: Cloud Stone
summary: A soft grey and brown stone with white flecks and a weathered, eroded surface. It reads as mountains and cliffs without the heavy contrast of darker rock, so it suits scapes where the plants should do the talking.
bestFor: Iwagumi and mountain-style layouts in 60 cm tanks and up, where you want enough stone for a full main-stone arrangement in one order.
highlights: Sold as a single 30 lb (about 13.6 kg) box of mixed sizes
Muted grey-brown colour with random white markings
Craggy, eroded texture that stacks into peaks
Works well with carpets, grasses and sandy paths

specs.Effect on water: Not stated by the seller; do a vinegar fizz test and check KH/GH before use
specs.Colour: Soft grey and brown with white markings
specs.Prep: Rinse and scrub well; the seller advises against boiling

watchOut: Only sold in a 30 lb lot, which is a lot of rock for a nano tank.

name: Cueva Stone
summary: A grey stone streaked with white and cream, with flecks of brown. It looks close to Ryuoh and Seiryu, with the same jagged texture that suits dynamic rockscapes.
bestFor: Iwagumi and rock-led layouts for keepers who want a Seiryu look with more white contrast.

specs.Effect on water: Not stated; Seiryu-like stones often raise KH and pH, so test before use
specs.Colour: Grey with white-cream striations and brown specks
specs.Prep: Rinse and scrub well before use

name: Dark Blue Slate Stone
summary: Flat blue-charcoal slate that turns much darker once wet. It stacks cleanly into caves and ledges and makes a stable base under driftwood.
bestFor: Stacked cave and ledge builds, and as a stable, hidden base for wood layouts.
highlights: Flat profile for stacking and caves
Easy to split into smaller pieces for moss stones

specs.Effect on water: Inert
specs.Prep: Rinse and scrub well before use

name: Desert Stone
summary: A golden-orange stone with scattered craters that looks a lot like Dragon (Ohko) stone. It is tougher and less crumbly than Ohko, so it throws off less dust, and the rough texture holds epiphytes well.
bestFor: Anyone who likes the Dragon stone look but wants a sturdier, cleaner-to-handle rock.
highlights: Golden orange colour, similar to Ohko
Less fragile and dusty than Dragon stone
Lava-like texture for moss and Bucephalandra

specs.Effect on water: Not stated by the seller; do a vinegar fizz test and check KH/GH before use
specs.Prep: Rinse and scrub well before use

name: Dragon Wood
summary: A driftwood with Malaysian-style colour and a pitted, holey surface like Dragon stone. Rhizome plants can often be pushed straight into the openings, no glue or thread needed.
bestFor: Scapes heavy on Bucephalandra, Anubias, Java Fern and moss that should look mature quickly.
highlights: Five sizes from about 8 cm to 61 cm+
Natural holes and cavities for planting

specs.Effect on water: Releases tannins, lowers pH slightly and tints the water
specs.Buoyancy: Not stated; soak before use
specs.Prep: Soak (or boil small pieces) until waterlogged; weigh down if it floats

name: Elephant Skin Stone
summary: Also called Seegebirge, Elephant Skin is a light grey stone with a wrinkled, leathery surface from years of erosion. It is rounded rather than sharp, which gives a softer look than Seiryu.
bestFor: Iwagumi or nature layouts that want strong texture with soft edges, especially with delicate-finned fish.
highlights: Light grey with deep wrinkles and grooves
Good for bettas and fancy goldfish

specs.Effect on water: Not stated; some batches nudge hardness up slightly, so test before use
specs.Prep: Rinse and scrub well before use

watchOut: Relatively expensive in the 20 and 30 lb lots.

name: Fire Stone
summary: A warm brown stone with a serrated, grippy texture full of crevices. It stacks well and suits caves, canyons and mountain terrain.
bestFor: Cave and canyon builds that need stones which lock together when stacked.
highlights: Serrated texture with lots of grip
Plenty of crevices for moss and plants

specs.Effect on water: Not stated by the seller; do a vinegar fizz test and check KH/GH before use
specs.Prep: Rinse and scrub well before use

name: Flat Bottom Dragon Ohko Stone
summary: Ohko (Dragon) stone formations with a cut flat base so they stand straight up without propping. Drop one in for an instant rock scape, or combine several for a bigger tank.
bestFor: Quick, stable rock layouts in small cubes (the seller pairs S with 25 cm and M with 30 cm cubes).
highlights: Two sizes, about 19 cm and 28 cm tall
Flat base, no need to wedge or glue
Classic Ohko scale texture and golden-brown colour
Tall enough to break the surface in small tanks

specs.Effect on water: Inert
specs.Prep: Rinse well to remove dust

watchOut: Each piece is unique and fairly pricey for the amount of stone.

name: Flat Bottom Seiryu Stone
summary: Seiryu formations cut with a flat base so they stand upright on their own. They give an instant Iwagumi-style centrepiece, and several can be grouped in larger tanks.
bestFor: Small cube Iwagumi builds where you want a stable peak without fiddling (S suits 25 cm cubes, M suits 30 cm cubes).
highlights: Two sizes, about 19 cm and 28 cm tall
Flat-cut base for easy, stable placement
Classic grey Seiryu grooves and peaks
Can poke above the waterline in small tanks

specs.Effect on water: Raises KH, GH and pH (calcareous, like all Seiryu-type stone)
specs.Prep: Rinse and scrub well before use

watchOut: Raises KH and pH like any Seiryu.

name: Forest Driftwood
summary: A relatively flat driftwood with deep grooves and mixed brown and beige tones. It works best as a base layer, or pieced together into intricate wood builds.
bestFor: Layered wood scapes and as a textured base under other hardscape.
highlights: Six sizes from about 10 cm to 74 cm

specs.Effect on water: Releases tannins, lowers pH slightly and tints the water
specs.Buoyancy: May float at first
specs.Prep: Soak (or boil small pieces) until waterlogged; weigh down if it floats

name: Ghost Wood
summary: Smooth, pale, sculptural branches with flowing lines. It is a statement wood that suits minimal scapes where stones hold it in place and negative space does the rest.
bestFor: Minimal, design-led nature layouts built around one or two feature branches.
highlights: Five sizes from under 25 cm to over 64 cm

specs.Effect on water: Releases tannins, lowers pH slightly and tints the water
specs.Buoyancy: Not stated; expect to weigh down or soak
specs.Prep: Soak (or boil small pieces) until waterlogged; weigh down if it floats

name: Goliath Stone
summary: Also sold as Rhino Stone, Goliath is grey and brown with plenty of texture but rounded rather than sharp. It suits the greening method, where moss is grown over the stone.
bestFor: Nature layouts with carpets or sand where you want chunky stones that moss can colonise.
highlights: Grey and brown with lots of surface texture
Rounded forms, kind to delicate fins
Good base under Malaysian or Spider Wood

specs.Effect on water: Not stated by the seller; do a vinegar fizz test and check KH/GH before use
specs.Prep: Rinse and scrub well before use

name: Grey River Slate
summary: Flat grey slate for stacking, building ledges or stabilising driftwood. It breaks easily into smaller pieces for foreground paths or moss stones.
bestFor: Stacked builds, caves, and as a stable base under wood layouts.

specs.Effect on water: Inert
specs.Prep: Rinse and scrub well before use

name: Hakkai Stone
summary: Also called Pa-Hai or bug-eaten stone, Hakkai is smooth and rounded with eroded pits and a blue, grey and green cast. It is one of the heaviest stones in the hobby, so a given weight buys fewer, smaller pieces.
bestFor: River-style scapes and calm Iwagumi with grassy plants like Dwarf Hairgrass or Blyxa.
highlights: 10, 20 and 30 lb lots plus a 5 lb bag of accent pieces
Smooth, rounded shape with natural pits and grooves
Safe for fancy goldfish and bettas thanks to soft edges

specs.Effect on water: Inert (per seller)
specs.Prep: Rinse and scrub well before use

watchOut: Very dense and pricey per kilo, so order more weight than your usual rule of thumb to get a spread of sizes.

name: Horn Wood
summary: Small, branchy pieces with a deep colour and lots of texture, sold in packs. They suit nano tanks on their own or perched on stone, and mix well with Pacific Wood.
bestFor: Nano tanks under about 40 litres, or as detail pieces in larger scapes.

specs.Effect on water: Releases tannins, lowers pH slightly and tints the water
specs.Buoyancy: May float at first
specs.Prep: Soak (or boil small pieces) until waterlogged; weigh down if it floats

name: Icelandic Lava Stone
summary: A lava rock with more character and texture than standard black lava, and slightly denser. It keeps the porous surface that epiphytes love while giving you craggier, more mountain-like shapes.
bestFor: Mountain-style scapes where you want the plant-friendliness of lava with more realistic rock shapes.
highlights: Rough texture that stacks with good grip

specs.Effect on water: Inert
specs.Prep: Rinse and scrub well before use

watchOut: Rough surface; keep long-finned fish in mind.

name: Jade Rhino Stone
summary: A rounded stone in muted jade green and blue-grey with patches of brown and cream. It has a gentle, river-worn look rather than sharp edges, which suits calm stream-style scapes.
bestFor: River and stream layouts with Eleocharis or other grassy plants, and tanks with delicate-finned fish.
highlights: Sold in 10 lb and 30 lb lots
Unusual green-blue colour for a scaping stone
Pairs well with light sand, pebbles and grassy plants

specs.Effect on water: Not stated by the seller; do a vinegar fizz test and check KH/GH before use
specs.Colour: Jade green and bluish grey with brown and cream patches
specs.Prep: Rinse and scrub well; the seller advises against boiling

name: Jade Stone
summary: A mostly smooth stone in cerulean, turquoise, jade and grey. The colour is subtle rather than loud, and works as either a feature stone or a support under wood.
bestFor: Scapers wanting a cool-toned, smooth stone that looks different from standard grey rock.
highlights: Blue, turquoise, jade and grey tones
Mostly smooth with a few textured patches
Deep hues contrast well with plants

specs.Effect on water: Not stated by the seller; do a vinegar fizz test and check KH/GH before use
specs.Prep: Rinse and scrub well before use

watchOut: Among the more expensive stones here per pound.

name: Joro Stone
summary: A distinctive purple-red stone with grey and cream veins running through it. It is an unusual colour in aquascaping and makes a strong statement in themed or nature-inspired scenes.
bestFor: Scapers after an uncommon colour to set a layout apart from the usual grey rock.
highlights: Deep purple-red with grey and cream striations
Blocky shapes that pair well with wood

specs.Effect on water: Not stated by the seller; do a vinegar fizz test and check KH/GH before use
specs.Colour: Purple-red with grey and cream veins
specs.Prep: Rinse and scrub well before use

name: Lagoon Stone
summary: A porous grey, white and black stone that sits between Wolf Stone and Icelandic lava. Its irregular shapes stack into larger structures and hold moss and epiphytes well.
bestFor: Moss-heavy scapes and stacked rock builds where the stone should be a focal point.

specs.Effect on water: Not stated; light porous rock like this is usually inert, but test before use
specs.Prep: Rinse and scrub well before use

watchOut: Quite rough, so not ideal with bettas or other long-finned fish.

name: Log Wood
summary: Straight, bark-textured log sections that read instantly as fallen trees. Lay them across the substrate for woodland scenes, or stand them up as trunks.
bestFor: Forest floor and fallen-tree scenes in aquariums.
highlights: Two diameters, both about 38-46 cm long
Bark texture takes moss and rhizome plants

specs.Effect on water: Releases tannins, lowers pH slightly and tints the water
specs.Buoyancy: May float at first
specs.Prep: Soak (or boil small pieces) until waterlogged; weigh down if it floats

name: Madra Wood
summary: A warm brown driftwood with lots of texture, knots and crevices, similar in look to Malaysian driftwood. It suits Anubias, Buce and Java Fern and works alone or perched on stone.
bestFor: Nature layouts wanting a Malaysian-style look, especially with epiphytes.
highlights: Three sizes from about 13 cm to 64 cm+

specs.Effect on water: Releases tannins, lowers pH slightly and tints the water
specs.Buoyancy: Not stated; soak before use
specs.Prep: Soak (or boil small pieces) until waterlogged; weigh down if it floats

name: Malaysian Driftwood
summary: One of the most recognisable aquascaping woods: dark, heavy and full of texture. It anchors nature-style layouts and usually sinks without much help, though it leaches plenty of tannin.
bestFor: Nature-style and blackwater-leaning tanks that want a statement piece of wood.
highlights: Four sizes from about 8 cm to 51 cm+, plus small accent stumps

specs.Effect on water: Releases tannins, lowers pH slightly and tints the water (quite strongly)
specs.Buoyancy: Usually sinks
specs.Prep: Soak or boil to reduce tannins before scaping

watchOut: Tannin release is heavy at first, so plan on water changes or carbon if you want clear water.

name: Manten Stone
summary: A rugged mountain stone with a very varied grey-brown palette. Its inconsistency is the point: no two pieces match, which helps build believable mini mountain scenes.
bestFor: Iwagumi and mountain layouts in soft-water or shrimp tanks where you want a natural-looking stone that leaves chemistry alone.
highlights: Varied grey, brown and tan tones
Inert, so safe for sensitive livestock

specs.Effect on water: Inert (per seller)
specs.Prep: Rinse and scrub well before use

name: Manzanita Wood
summary: Natural (not sandblasted) manzanita with smooth, stiff bark and classic branching. Use a branch piece for a standard tank or the twig piece for nanos, and tie moss over cut ends.
bestFor: Tree and forest scenes in long rimless or standard tanks (Branch) and nanos (Twig).

specs.Effect on water: Releases tannins, lowers pH slightly and tints the water
specs.Buoyancy: Floats at first; soak before use
specs.Prep: Soak (or boil small pieces) until waterlogged; weigh down if it floats

name: Maple Stone
summary: A porous stone in deep red-brown tones, not often seen in planted tanks. Moss, Anubias and Bucephalandra will eventually attach to it on their own.
bestFor: Scapers wanting an uncommon warm-coloured stone for nature layouts.

specs.Effect on water: Not stated by the seller; do a vinegar fizz test and check KH/GH before use
specs.Prep: Rinse and scrub well before use

name: Marsh Stone
summary: A light grey, softly rounded stone with cream and white hints, similar in feel to Hakkai. It still has grooves and cracks for moss and epiphytes but no sharp edges.
bestFor: Calm Iwagumi or community tanks that want a Hakkai-like look at a lower price.
highlights: Light grey with cream and white

specs.Effect on water: Not stated by the seller; do a vinegar fizz test and check KH/GH before use
specs.Colour: Light grey with cream and white
specs.Prep: Rinse and scrub well before use

name: Mopani Wood
summary: A dense African hardwood with a two-tone light and dark brown finish, knots and gnarled shapes. It sinks quickly and lasts for years, but it leaches a lot of tannin.
bestFor: Blackwater, African biotope and long-term layouts where you want wood that sinks with little fuss.
highlights: Three sizes from about 18 cm to 56 cm
Heavy and dense, sinks far sooner than most driftwood
Very durable and slow to break down

specs.Effect on water: Releases a lot of tannin, lowers pH slightly and stains the water
specs.Buoyancy: Sinks quickly
specs.Prep: Pre-soak for several days to cut the tannin release

watchOut: Expect tea-coloured water for weeks unless you pre-soak or run carbon.

name: Mountain Stone
summary: A light, porous brown stone with a gritty surface that grips well. Because it is low density you get more pieces per pound than with Seiryu or Hakkai.
bestFor: Cliff and canyon scapes that need lots of stone without lots of weight on the glass.
highlights: Stacks well for cliffs, caves and canyons

specs.Effect on water: Not stated; light porous rock like this is usually inert, but test before use
specs.Prep: Rinse and scrub well before use

name: Ohko Dragon Stone
summary: Ohko, better known as Dragon stone, is a light clay-based rock with a scaly texture in brown and golden orange. It is easy to stack, easy to break into smaller pieces, and one of the few natural rocks that leaves water chemistry alone.
bestFor: Beginners and shrimp keepers who want a characterful, inert stone for nature or Iwagumi layouts.
highlights: 5, 10 and 16 lb lots plus a 2 lb bag of small accent pieces
Warm brown and orange scale-like texture
Lightweight and easy to break down
Nooks for moss and shelter for shrimp

specs.Effect on water: Inert
specs.Prep: Rinse well; pockets hold clay and dust

watchOut: Fragile and dusty, and clay trapped in the holes can cloud a fresh tank if not rinsed out.

name: Pacific Wood
summary: An easy, versatile driftwood with rich brown colour, knots and grooves. It is denser than branchy woods, so it waterlogs faster, and the stump pieces make solid foundations for bigger builds.
bestFor: Beginners and nature-style scapers in any tank size, from nano Bucephalandra gardens to large layouts.
highlights: Branch pieces from about 10 cm to 66 cm+, plus chunky stump pieces
Denser than branchy woods, quicker to waterlog
Knots and grooves hold Anubias, Buce, moss and ferns

specs.Effect on water: Releases tannins, lowers pH slightly and tints the water
specs.Buoyancy: Waterlogs faster than most; may need a brief soak
specs.Prep: Soak (or boil small pieces) until waterlogged; weigh down if it floats

name: Patagonia Stone
summary: A soft brown stone full of pores and holes, similar in texture to lava rock. The pitted surface is ideal for moss and epiphytes to grip onto.
bestFor: Low-tech and nature-style tanks where you plan to cover the stone with moss, Anubias or Bucephalandra.
highlights: Very porous with pockets and crevices
Stacks easily and works as a base for wood

specs.Effect on water: Not stated; light porous rock like this is usually inert, but test before use
specs.Prep: Rinse and scrub well before use

name: Petrified Wood Stone
summary: Fossilised wood that has turned to stone, so it looks like layered timber but behaves like rock. The banded brown, tan and grey tones work well alongside real driftwood.
bestFor: Nature-style scapes that want a stone which ties visually into the wood.

specs.Effect on water: Generally inert (silica based)
specs.Prep: Rinse and scrub well before use

watchOut: Very heavy for its size, so protect the glass when placing big pieces.

name: Red Manten Stone
summary: A red-brown take on Manten, with orange, cream and beige showing in its weathered cracks. The warm colour contrasts strongly with green plants and looks at home in canyon and hillside scapes.
bestFor: Warm-toned canyon or rocky hillside layouts, or anyone wanting a change from grey stone.
highlights: Deep reddish brown with orange and cream markings
Useful as a support stone under driftwood

specs.Effect on water: Not stated by the seller; do a vinegar fizz test and check KH/GH before use
specs.Colour: Reddish brown with orange, cream and beige
specs.Prep: Rinse and scrub well; the seller advises against boiling

name: Ryuoh Stone
summary: Sometimes sold as boutique Seiryu, Ryuoh is a charcoal grey stone with white marbling, deep grooves and jagged edges. It is medium weight: lighter than Hakkai, denser than lava.
bestFor: Iwagumi layouts where you want a darker, more dramatic alternative to standard Seiryu.
highlights: Clean lines and sharp grooves for Iwagumi
Solid base for driftwood in nature layouts

specs.Effect on water: Not stated; Seiryu-like stones usually raise KH and pH, so test before use
specs.Prep: Rinse and scrub well before use

watchOut: Expect it to behave like Seiryu and harden the water unless your own test says otherwise.

name: Sand Stone
summary: A warm beige and cream stone with horizontal layered striations, like a weathered cliff face. It stacks easily and gives a softer, warmer palette than grey rock.
bestFor: Warm-toned cliff, clearing or beach-style layouts, especially paired with driftwood.
highlights: Layered striations for cliff and ridge looks
Mix of flat and taller angular pieces

specs.Effect on water: Not stated by the seller; do a vinegar fizz test and check KH/GH before use
specs.Prep: Rinse and scrub well before use

watchOut: Sandstone can be bound with calcium carbonate, so test it if you keep soft-water species.

name: Sandblasted Manzanita Driftwood
summary: Very branchy manzanita that has been sandblasted to a smooth, even pale finish. It builds tree and forest scenes easily and looks good bare or covered in moss.
bestFor: Tree-style and forest layouts, from small cubes up to large display tanks.
highlights: Five sizes from about 15 cm to over 90 cm

specs.Effect on water: Releases tannins, lowers pH slightly and tints the water
specs.Colour: Pale tan, turns browner once wet
specs.Buoyancy: Floats at first; soak before use
specs.Prep: Soak (or boil small pieces) until waterlogged; weigh down if it floats

watchOut: Thin branches snap easily in transit and when scaping.

name: Seiryu Base Stone
summary: A 20 lb selection of long, flat, slab-like Seiryu pieces meant for building structure rather than as feature stones. Use them as retaining walls, supports under main stones and wood, or to shape slopes.
bestFor: Sloped or terraced Iwagumi and nature layouts that need hidden structure beneath the show stones.
highlights: Same grey colour and texture as standard Seiryu
Good for terraces, retaining walls and substrate transitions

specs.Effect on water: Raises KH, GH and pH (calcareous, like all Seiryu-type stone)
specs.Colour: Classic Seiryu grey with white veining
specs.Prep: Rinse and scrub well before use

watchOut: Not meant as main stones, and like all Seiryu it pushes up hardness, so it is a poor fit for soft-water shrimp.

name: Seiryu Stone
summary: The classic Iwagumi stone: blue-grey with white veins, sharp ridges and deep grooves. It comes in every size from nano pebbles to big main stones and works just as well at the foot of driftwood.
bestFor: Iwagumi and nature layouts in tanks where a little extra hardness is fine, such as most community fish and Neocaridina setups.
highlights: 5, 10, 20 and 30 lb lots plus a 3 lb bag of small accent pieces
Jagged, grooved shapes with lots of character
Suits tanks from 4 litre cubes to large standards

specs.Effect on water: Raises KH, GH and pH (calcareous, like all Seiryu-type stone)
specs.Prep: Rinse and scrub well before use

watchOut: Raises KH and pH over time, so it is a poor choice for Caridina shrimp or soft-water specialists.

name: Spider Wood
summary: The go-to branchy wood: a tangle of twisting, root-like branches with endless places to tie moss and epiphytes. It starts pale and darkens once waterlogged, and the Nano pieces add root detail in small tanks.
bestFor: Forest, root and bonsai-inspired layouts in any tank size, often perched on Dragon stone or Seiryu.
highlights: Sizes from about 8 cm (Nano) to 61 cm+ (XL)
Ideal for bonsai-style and forest scapes

specs.Effect on water: Releases tannins, lowers pH slightly and tints the water
specs.Colour: Pale tan, darkens to brown when wet
specs.Buoyancy: Floats until waterlogged; weigh down or soak
specs.Prep: Soak (or boil small pieces) until waterlogged; weigh down if it floats

watchOut: Expect a week or two of floating and a harmless white fungal film early on.

name: Spider Wood on Slate Stone
summary: Spider wood already fixed to a flat slate base, so it goes straight into the tank without floating. Bury the slate under soil or let it show and add stones around it.
bestFor: Beginners and quick setups that want branchy wood without the floating problem.
highlights: Five sizes from about 18 cm to 71 cm
Pre-attached slate base keeps the wood down

specs.Effect on water: Releases tannins, lowers pH slightly and tints the water
specs.Colour: Light brown wood on grey slate
specs.Buoyancy: Held down by slate base
specs.Prep: Rinse; ready to use

watchOut: Branch shape is fixed to the base, so you have less freedom to angle the wood.

name: Star Wood
summary: Long, fairly straight branches with pointed tips, somewhere between Manzanita and Spider Wood. The predictable shape makes it easier to build clean triangular or central compositions.
bestFor: Wood-focused nature layouts in standard and larger tanks that need structured, directional lines.
highlights: Three sizes from about 41 cm to 71 cm+
Takes rhizome plants and moss well

specs.Effect on water: Releases tannins, lowers pH slightly and tints the water
specs.Buoyancy: Floats at first; weigh down or soak
specs.Prep: Soak (or boil small pieces) until waterlogged; weigh down if it floats

watchOut: Expect harmless white biofilm for the first few weeks.

name: Strata Pro Hardscape
summary: Ready-made layouts of real Dragon stone, with or without bonsai driftwood, fixed to a resin mat and sized for 36, 45 and 60 cm rimless tanks. You see exactly what you get, drop it in, add soil and plants, and the hardscape is done.
bestFor: Beginners or busy keepers with a 36, 45 or 60 cm tank who want a finished, balanced hardscape without choosing and gluing stones.
highlights: 17 designs built from natural Dragon stone, many with bonsai driftwood
Sized for 36 cm (Pro 5), 45 cm (Pro 45) and 60 cm (Pro 60) tanks
Everything is fixed to a resin base mat
Suggested planting: Anubias, Bucephalandra, Cryptocoryne and moss

specs.Effect on water: Dragon stone is inert; designs with wood release some tannins
specs.Colour: Golden-brown Dragon stone, brown bonsai wood
specs.Pro 5 size: about 28 x 18 x 20 cm, for 36 cm tanks
specs.Pro 45 size: about 38 x 23 x 25 cm, for 45 cm tanks
specs.Pro 60 size: about 58 x 28 x 30 cm, for 60 cm tanks
specs.Prep: Rinse before placing

watchOut: Expensive compared with buying loose stone and wood, and the layout is fixed, so there is no rearranging later.

name: Strata Seiryu Hardscape
summary: One-piece Iwagumi rock formations cast in lightweight aquarium-safe resin to look like Seiryu stone. Type 1 is taller and more dramatic, Type 2 is lower and more open to leave room for a carpet.
bestFor: First Iwagumi builds in 20-40 litre tanks, and soft-water shrimp keepers who love the Seiryu look but not its effect on KH.
highlights: Seiryu look without the hardness increase
Sized for UNS 5N and 45U tanks; both together suit a 60U
Safe for fish, shrimp and plants

specs.Effect on water: None (resin)

watchOut: It is resin, not real stone, and up close it will not have the variation of natural rock.

name: Striped River Stone
summary: Smooth, rounded river stones with striped patterns in white, grey, brown and orange. They look natural in river layouts and are safe around delicate fins.
bestFor: River-style scapes and tanks with fancy goldfish or bettas.
highlights: Pairs well with sand and simple planting

specs.Effect on water: Not stated by the seller; do a vinegar fizz test and check KH/GH before use
specs.Colour: White, grey, brown and orange stripes
specs.Prep: Rinse and scrub well before use

name: Thorn Wood
summary: Straight sticks covered in short side spikes. Underwater the spikes read as tiny horizontal branches, which is great for creating depth in forest scapes, especially with moss tied on.
bestFor: Forest-style layouts built from many vertical stems.
highlights: Straight stems with thorn-like side spurs
Takes moss well for underwater forests

specs.Effect on water: Releases tannins, lowers pH slightly and tints the water (quite strongly)
specs.Buoyancy: Floats; soak, boil or weigh down
specs.Prep: Soak (or boil small pieces) until waterlogged; weigh down if it floats

name: Tree Branch Driftwood
summary: Very branchy pieces with clusters of fine twigs, made for cascading tree and forest looks. Tie moss onto the twigs for an underwater canopy.
bestFor: Underwater tree scapes in nano to standard tanks (Nano for about 15-40 L, Medium for 40-75 L, Large for 75 L+).
highlights: Nano, Medium and Large sizes, about 10-46 cm
Good anchor for moss and small epiphytes
Seller sizes it to tank volume

specs.Effect on water: Releases tannins, lowers pH slightly and tints the water
specs.Buoyancy: Floats at first; soak or weigh down
specs.Prep: Soak (or boil small pieces) until waterlogged; weigh down if it floats

name: Tree Root Driftwood
summary: Pale, forked root pieces that mimic the root system of a tree, in a standard and a more tangled version. Both suit tied-on moss or ferns wedged into the forks.
bestFor: Root-style details and small tree scenes in nano to mid-sized tanks.
highlights: Tangled version with denser, gnarled roots
Sinks on its own in about two weeks

specs.Effect on water: Releases tannins, lowers pH slightly and tints the water
specs.Buoyancy: Usually sinks by itself within about two weeks
specs.Prep: Soak (or boil small pieces) until waterlogged; weigh down if it floats

watchOut: Some sharp tips, so soften them with moss if you keep bettas.

name: Verdant Stone
summary: A muted grey-blue stone with grey-cream veins and the odd rust speck. It has a texture much like Seiryu, which holds moss well.
bestFor: Scapers wanting a cooler blue-grey stone for Iwagumi or as a base under wood.
highlights: Works as a driftwood base or in Iwagumi

specs.Effect on water: Not stated by the seller; do a vinegar fizz test and check KH/GH before use
specs.Colour: Grey-blue with grey-cream veins and rust specks
specs.Prep: Rinse and scrub well before use

name: White Elephant Skin Stone
summary: A cream and beige version of Elephant Skin, with the same wrinkled, grooved surface and soft edges. The light colour stands out against dark soil and green carpets.
bestFor: Bright, high-contrast scapes over dark soil or carpets, and tanks with delicate-finned fish.
highlights: Cream and beige rather than grey
Smooth edges, safe for bettas and goldfish

specs.Effect on water: Not stated by the seller; do a vinegar fizz test and check KH/GH before use
specs.Prep: Rinse and scrub well before use

watchOut: Light stone shows algae easily and is pricey in the larger lots.

name: Wolf Stone
summary: Something of a cross between Elephant Skin and Icelandic lava: grey, sharper and more jagged than Elephant Skin, and fairly porous. Moss and epiphytes attach readily.
bestFor: Nature layouts where the stone will carry mosses like Christmas, Pellia or Fissidens.
highlights: Good for an aged, moss-covered look

specs.Effect on water: Not stated; light porous rock like this is usually inert, but test before use
specs.Prep: Rinse and scrub well before use

name: Yukon Canyon Stone
summary: An earthy stone that ranges from grey to golden brown and beige. Its semi-flat, rounded pieces stack stably and blend into biotope and nature layouts.
bestFor: Biotope and nature-style tanks that want a neutral, earthy base stone under wood.
highlights: Mixed grey, golden brown and beige tones
Semi-flat, rounded pieces that stack well

specs.Effect on water: Not stated by the seller; do a vinegar fizz test and check KH/GH before use
specs.Prep: Rinse and scrub well before use
